approval.approval_reference: User approval 2026-08-11 JST: retain all six July Special themes within 32-40 pages if feasible; prioritize Frontier Models, then Multimodal, followed by Inference/Serving, Agents, Safety/Security, and Paper Watch. ChatGPT confirmed a coherent 36-page single-volume architecture is feasible.

FEATURE_CORE.title: Claude Opus 5
FEATURE_CORE.selection_rationale: Top-priority Frontier Models comparison point: Claude Opus 5 is a major July frontier release with clear availability and pricing chronology.
remaining_boundaries: Benchmark and alignment comparisons are primarily Anthropic-reported; individual evaluation harnesses and partner testimonials are not equivalent to independent replication.

FEATURE_CORE.title: GPT-5.6 family
FEATURE_CORE.selection_rationale: Top-priority Frontier Models anchor: a major July family launch spanning ChatGPT, Codex and API, with follow-up pricing changes.
remaining_boundaries: Benchmark, efficiency, and estimated-cost comparisons are largely vendor-reported and depend on effort levels, harnesses, token usage, and pricing assumptions; they should not be flattened into a universal ranking.

FEATURE_CORE.title: Kimi K3
FEATURE_CORE.selection_rationale: Top-priority Frontier Models item with open-weight significance and direct coding-agent integration, useful for continuity with later model/ecosystem Specials.
remaining_boundaries: Architecture scale, capability comparisons, and benchmark positioning are vendor claims from the Kimi documentation; open-source status should be interpreted using the actual published license/weights when drafting.

FEATURE_CORE.title: MiniMax H3
FEATURE_CORE.selection_rationale: Top-priority Multimodal anchor: MiniMax H3 is the strongest July unified multimodal-generation launch in the reviewed evidence.
remaining_boundaries: Generation quality and capability examples are vendor demonstrations; the announcement explicitly described weight publication as planned rather than complete at that moment.

PAPER_WATCH.title: DiffusionGemma
PAPER_WATCH.selection_rationale: Retain the sixth theme at deliberately lower priority: DiffusionGemma is a notable alternative-generation paper, but author-reported results do not justify displacing model or ecosystem coverage.
remaining_boundaries: The technical report is an author-controlled evaluation of an experimental model; speed and quality results depend on its sampler, model configuration, and hardware setup.

SECTION_CORE.title: Alibaba Model Studio July multimodal updates
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Multimodal section core: Qwen-Audio 3.0 and Wan 2.7 provide primary-source July audio/video model chronology and Chinese-ecosystem continuity.
remaining_boundaries: Availability is region-specific and the performance/quality descriptions are vendor claims from Alibaba Cloud Model Studio.

SECTION_CORE.title: DeepSeek V4-Flash July API lifecycle
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Frontier Models section core: DeepSeek V4-Flash public beta and API lifecycle changes capture an important July Chinese-model transition.
remaining_boundaries: DeepSeek's benchmark scores for V4-Flash are vendor-reported and include a specified DeepSeek Harness configuration; this card treats the July lifecycle and API change as the primary fact.

SECTION_CORE.title: FlashInfer July MoE/Blackwell serving releases
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Inference/Serving core: FlashInfer's July MoE, expert-parallel and Blackwell work shows the hardware/runtime layer moving with frontier models.
remaining_boundaries: Hardware/model support is highly GPU-generation-specific, and any throughput numbers in release notes are project benchmarks rather than general serving guarantees.

SECTION_CORE.title: Gemini API July model lifecycle
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Frontier Models section core: Gemini 3.6 Flash GA and related July lifecycle changes provide a major Google comparison point.
remaining_boundaries: Capability/efficiency positioning is Google-reported; the July release-notes page establishes model lifecycle and availability rather than independent benchmark superiority.

SECTION_CORE.title: GPT-Live
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Multimodal section core: GPT-Live represents real-time simultaneous listening/speaking and connects live interaction to frontier-model delegation.
remaining_boundaries: Availability and latency/capability statements originate from OpenAI; independent real-time quality evaluation is not established by this source.

SECTION_CORE.title: July agent injection and MCP security research
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Safety/Security core: multiple July studies expose distinct injection, tool-schema, audio and MCP attack surfaces; threat models must remain separated.
remaining_boundaries: Each result has a distinct threat model and evaluation setup; the papers should not be merged into a single universal 'agents are unsafe' claim.

SECTION_CORE.title: July long-horizon agent evaluation research
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Agents core: July evaluation research moves beyond isolated coding tasks toward sustained loops and streaming adaptation.
remaining_boundaries: Both benchmark designs and reported model rankings/results are author-reported; conclusions depend on the included harnesses, models, task sources, and scoring protocols.

SECTION_CORE.title: July persistent-agent memory safety research
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Safety/Security core: persistent memory introduces a new control plane around rollback, provenance and authority preservation.
remaining_boundaries: These are research prototypes/benchmarks with author-reported evaluations; production effectiveness across arbitrary memory backends and agents is not independently established.

SECTION_CORE.title: Long-horizon model safety and alignment
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Safety/Security core: concrete July operational learning about long-horizon model failure modes and trajectory-level monitoring.
remaining_boundaries: The incident evidence is reported by OpenAI about its internal environment; the source does not establish prevalence across independent deployments.

SECTION_CORE.title: OpenAI–Hugging Face evaluation security incident
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Safety/Security core: a concrete evaluation-infrastructure security incident provides an operational counterpart to research threat models.
remaining_boundaries: The event occurred under a deliberately permissive cybersecurity evaluation configuration; it should not be generalized to normal product behavior or described as an unrestricted sandbox escape.

SECTION_CORE.title: SGLang July releases
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Inference/Serving core: July SGLang releases changed speculative-decoding defaults and introduced DSpark.
remaining_boundaries: Reported throughput/TPS figures are project benchmarks under specific batch size, tensor-parallel, model, and GPU configurations.

SECTION_CORE.title: vLLM July releases
SECTION_CORE.selection_rationale: Inference/Serving core: July vLLM releases changed the default dense-model execution path and expanded frontier-model support.
remaining_boundaries: Performance percentages in release notes are project measurements for specific kernels/models; integration support does not by itself prove model quality or availability outside vLLM.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: July agent-serving systems research
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Support the Agents section with KV reuse, sandbox prewarming and tokenization-system evidence rather than creating a separate systems-paper story.
remaining_boundaries: The systems gains are author-reported and depend on analytical/microbenchmark assumptions, workload traces, serving stack, and hardware.

SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.title: July diffusion/MoE inference research
SUPPORTING_EVIDENCE.selection_rationale: Use FlashDiff/EcoSpec research to explain emerging diffusion and MoE serving concepts without spending a separate article package on author-evaluated papers.
remaining_boundaries: Both are author-evaluated systems papers; reported gains depend on their selected models, hardware, workloads, and baselines.

not_selected_for_architecture.title: Z.AI release chronology
not_selected_for_architecture.selection_rationale: Evidence Runner recommendation is REJECT; re-verify Evidence before promotion.
remaining_boundaries: Weekly why-now relevance is not confirmed.

Absence from this official release-notes page does not prove that no Z.AI-related activity occurred elsewhere; it is sufficient only to reject this index snapshot as evidence for a July release story.

rules: Issue Architecture may group several selected items into one comparison package.
Supporting evidence is not a duplicate story and need not receive its own article package.
Do not add HOLD_OUT or EXCLUDE items without a new Selection revision bound to an updated matrix.
No section quota is required; weak sections may be omitted.
Article drafting begins only after the Architecture Plan validates successfully.
